thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: service-discovery.srv-errors > 5% (us-west-2a). High SRV lookup failures observed for internal inference-backend SRV queries. Auto-escalation to on-call.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident #INC-5621 triggered — on-call: alex.
alex: ack — I'm on it. observing spikes in SRV_LOOKUP_FAIL for inference-backend across multiple clusters in us-west-2a.
alex: quick check: is this limited to CoreDNS or do we see consul/etcd anomalies?
Priya Patel: checking consul health now. early look — consul leader flapped around the same time on node consul-3 in us-west-2a, some rpc timeouts.
Jamal Reyes: I can pull CoreDNS logs and kube-proxy stats. Might be a cache/regeneration loop in the coredns cache plugin causing lots of SERVFAILs.
Sara Kim: Customer impact — internal monitoring shows increased 5xx for hosted inference routes for ~30% of requests hitting us-west-2a. A few enterprise customers report errors on model loads. Tracking acme-corp and beta-incidents.
alex: mitigation plan ideas: 1) scale up coredns replicas in affected k8s clusters 2) restart consul agent on consul-3 3) temporarily route inference traffic away from us-west-2a via smart routing policy (canary to us-west-2b)
Priya Patel: agreed. I'll take consul restart and health checks. Jamal, can you do the CoreDNS scale + rolling restart?
Jamal Reyes: on it. running:
```
kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy coredns --replicas=5 --context=us-west-2a
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deploy coredns --context=us-west-2a
```
I'm also tailing logs: `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/coredns -f`

eng-sre: note: runbook step PRD-DNS-1 suggests checking negative-cache TTL and watch for excessive cache evictions. If TTL very low (<=1s) that can cause regen storms.

Priya Patel: consul-3 restart scheduled now (drain -> restart agent -> verify raft). Command: `systemctl restart consul` on consul-3. I'll monitor `consul operator raft list-peers` and `consul members`.

Priya Patel: update: consul restarted; raft stabilized, node back in quorum. Some SRV errors dropping but still elevated.

Jamal Reyes: CoreDNS replicas scaled and rolled. Logs show repeated "cache: negative cache update" messages then SERVFAIL from consul upstream. Increasing cache TTL to 15s as temporary patch. Applying configmap patch now.

Jamal Reyes: applying config: `kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap coredns -p 'data: {"cache.ttl": "15"}'` then rollout restart.

alex: I'm going to enable routing policy to prefer us-west-2b for inference-backend traffic (5-minute window) to reduce customer impact. Rolling that now.

alex: route flip in console applied: inference-backend -> prefer us-west-2b, fallback us-west-2a. Monitoring error rates.

Sara Kim: customer comms: opening a short status note to impacted customers. Notifying acme-corp support with ETA ~15m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation actions applied: consul restart, CoreDNS scale+ttl increase, routing preference change. Continued monitoring.

Jamal Reyes: post-change logs look quieter. SRV lookup error rate trending down from 6.2% -> 0.9% over 10m.

Priya Patel: consul metrics stable. No further leader flaps. Network metrics show increased latency on consul-3's machine before restart — looks like intermittent NIC driver hiccup. Filing infra ticket IR-349 to replace host.

alex: handing off to Priya for overnight watch. Priya, you're primary. I'll be reachable if anything regresses.

Priya Patel: accepted handoff. Will keep monitoring for the next 3 hours and then hand to next oncall (Jamal).

Sara Kim: summary for postmortem: root cause likely transient NIC/host issue causing consul agent instability -> SRV upstream errors -> CoreDNS cache regen storm amplifying failures -> partial customer impact. Action items: replace host, add automated host NIC checks, add a safer default for coredns cache TTL, add routing fallback to non-affected AZ sooner in playbooks.

alex: agree. assigning action items: infra to replace host (Jamal to own IR-349), eng-sre to add TTL guard (alex), product to draft customer follow-up (Sara).

Priya Patel: monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to avoid noise but still catch real regressions. Will post timeline in #postmortems after investigation.

Sara Kim: customer note posted: short explanation + mitigation + ETA for full postmortem. Mentioned affected customers and open support links.

eng-sre: closing note: mark incident status = mitigated. Recommend 72h watch on service-discovery metrics.

alex: thanks team. leaving thread open for follow-up docs.

Priya Patel: closing ack.
